paper.title_en: Strongly Suppressed Cosmic-Ray Diffusion in a Wind-Blown Cavity Environment of SNR G21.8-3.0
paper.abstract_en: We report the discovery of a GeV $γ$-ray source spatially offset from SNR G21.8-3.0, while no significant high-energy emission is detected from the remnant itself. Using 16 yr of \emph{Fermi}-LAT observations together with $^{12}$CO ($J=1-0$) data, we show that the GeV emission is spatially associated with a localized molecular cloud located just outside a gas cavity whose boundary closely follows the SNR shell. This configuration supports a scenario in which cosmic rays (CRs) escaping from the remnant propagate through a progenitor-carved low-density cavity and illuminate nearby dense gas. Modeling of the cloud emission requires a diffusion coefficient suppressed by a factor of several tens relative to the canonical Galactic value, indicating strongly inhibited CR transport around the remnant. Rather than serving as a simple low-density escape channel, the wind-blown cavity appears to regulate CR propagation through local magnetic structure and enhanced turbulence. This system therefore provides evidence that circumstellar structures can control the escape and early transport of CRs around supernova remnants.
